focus: how the application market treats the release-age cooldown, and what that implies for release timing

coexistence.marketUi: 已安装 view lists dsh-review-outbox with its description; both bundles load with no page errors

marketSideCooldown.behaviour: The market computes latestMaturityAt and nextMaturityAt, and marks a newer version as held while it is still inside the release-age window, with an estimated maturity time when the registry cannot say.
marketSideCooldown.consequence: The 'why do I still get the old version' symptom authors hit with dsh plugin add is the same policy the market already surfaces as a pending update.
marketSideCooldown.verified: read from the installed bundle source; the UI message itself was not driven

publishWindowRule.why: the next daily build then lands after the cooldown expires, so the card version and the resolvable version agree for the whole day
publishWindowRule.counterExample: publishing late in the evening leaves the catalog showing the new version while installs still resolve the previous one, for up to about a day

releaseTimelineForDailyProfile.note: a caret range resolves to the highest matured version, so the daily profile reaches 0.1.4 first and 0.1.6 a day later, without any manual step
